[[File:Morgan Crofton.jpeg|thumb|Morgan Crofton]]

'''Morgan William Crofton''' (1826, [[Dublin]], Ireland – 1915, [[Brighton]], England) was an Irish mathematician who contributed to the field of [[integral geometry|geometric probability theory]]. He also worked with [[James Joseph Sylvester]] and contributed an article on probability to the 9th edition of the ''[[Encyclopædia Britannica]]''. [[Crofton's formula]] is named in his honour.

==Early life==
Morgan Crofton was born into a wealthy [[Anglo-Irish]] family. His father, the [[Reverend]] William Crofton, [[Rector (ecclesiastical)|Rector of]] [[Skreen]], [[County Sligo]], was the younger brother of [[Crofton baronets|Sir Malby Crofton]], [[Baronet|2nd Baronet]] of Longford House.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Crofton.html |title=Crofton biography |website=www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060505000631/http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Biographies/Crofton.html |archive-date=5 May 2006 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also the cousin of [[Edward Crofton, 2nd Baron Crofton|Lord Edward Crofton]], [[Baron Crofton]] of the Mote.  Despite being born into an [[aristocratic]], [[Anglican]] family, Crofton joined to the [[Roman Catholic Church]] in the 1850s in part due to an interest in [[Cardinal Newman|Cardinal John Henry Newman]]. 
This led to his resignation at [[National University of Ireland, Galway|Queen's College, Galway]] and transference to various Catholic colleges.

He married twice: firstly on 31 August 1857 Julia Agnes Cecilia, daughter of J B Kernan (died 1902) and secondly Katherine, daughter of Holland Taylor of Manchester.

==Career==
He was Professor of Mathematics at the [[Royal Military Academy, Woolwich]] and Professor of Natural Philosophy at [[Queen's University of Ireland]]. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in June, 1868.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://makingscience.royalsociety.org/people/na8050/morgan-william-crofton|title=Morgan William Crofton|publisher=The Royal Society|work=Science in the Making|access-date=2025-09-04}}</ref>
